descriptionChirho: A large, solid mass of stone; used both of literal geological rock formations (Matt 27:51 rocks splitting, Matt 27:60 tomb hewn from rock, Rev 6:15-16 hiding among rocks) and metaphorically of a firm foundation for building (Matt 7:24-25 house on rock, Matt 16:18 'on this rock I will build my church,' 1 Cor 10:4 the spiritual rock). Distinguished from πέτρος (a detachable stone) by denoting massive, immovable bedrock. Multilingual evidence confirms a single sense: spa 'roca/piedra/peñas,' hin 'चट्टान/चट्टानों' (caṭṭān), arb 'صَخرَة/صُخور' (ṣaḫra/ṣuḫūr), kor '바위/반석' (bawi/banseok — rock/bedrock), swa 'mwamba/miamba.' Singular and plural forms reflect grammatical number, not distinct meanings.
